faq.a: Cyrus is associated with the Persian form كُورُوش, whose core sense is cyrus; a persian royal name.

faq.q: What is the origin of Cyrus?
faq.a: Cyrus is associated with Persian. Cyrus is Persian کوروش (Kūrush), the name of the founder of the Achaemenid Empire. It is used as a male given name in Iran.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Cyrus can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Cyrus should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Kūrush is a Persian name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
